speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger in detail, including when it started and if you have any history of similar episodes.

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism of injury sounds very suspicious for a dislocation or fracture. Did the finger get stuck in a bent position when it was pulled, and have you noticed any obvious deformity or inability to move the joint since the injury?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to flex your distal interphalangeal joint and the finger remaining extended at rest are classic signs of a "mallet finger." Given the history of forced hyperextension, is there any numbness or tingling in your finger, and can you still make a fist with the other fingers? REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-ray.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Closed Extensor Tendon Injury of the Distal Interphalangeal Joint). The clinical presentation of an inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint, the finger resting in extension, and the history of forced hyperextension during a sports injury are pathognomonic for this condition. While I have requested X-ray images to rule out an associated avulsion fracture or dislocation, the functional deficit confirms the primary diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
